title: Beylik of Karasi
capsule: The Beylik of Karasi was one of the Anatolian beyliks that emerged from the fragmentation of Seljuk and Mongol power after the Mongol victory at Köse Dağ (1243), controlling the Mysia region of northwestern Anatolia — roughly modern Balıkesir and Çanakkale provinces — including the ancient sites of Pergamon and Adramyttium. Founded by Kalem Bey around 1303–1305, the beylik mounted significant naval raids into Thrace and the Aegean, making it a notable maritime power. Orhan absorbed Karasi around 1345–1360 by exploiting dynastic succession disputes, making it one of the earliest beyliks incorporated into the nascent Ottoman state; former Karasi commanders including Hacı İlbey subsequently led early Ottoman operations in the Balkans.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The beylik's core territory in Mysia is established through Ottoman and Byzantine chronicles, but precise boundaries with neighbouring beyliks such as Saruhan and Germiyan are not sharply defined in contemporary sources.
